purpose: Describe how supported declines in effective breeding-component number were produced internally, without creating a new inferential endpoint.

initial_dominant: identity of the breeding component with the largest share in the first eligible season
final_dominant: identity of the breeding component with the largest share in the last eligible season
its first-season share and initial rank
component_trajectories: OLS slope of log1p breeding-pair count against actual year
outputs.descriptive_association: Spearman rank correlation between first-season share and component log1p-count slope within each population; report rho only, no p-value or confidence interval.

interpretation_rules: N_eff decline alone does not imply that initially large components persist.
Use 'large-group refuge' language only if the descriptive trajectories actually show initially large groups declining more slowly.
Use 'dominance turnover' language only when the identity of the largest component changes between the first and last eligible seasons.
No descriptive pattern may replace, rescue, or modify the frozen concentration inference.
Do not pool the five populations into a new significance test.

palmer.LIT: 1991 through final positive census in 2006, unchanged nine-code roster

signy_adelie.canonicalization: A1, A60, A1 + A60 and A1+A60 are summed into A1+A60
